Think about the cost of each option if it fails, not just if it succeeds. Which option leaves you with something — an offer, a relationship, an alternative — if the primary goal does not work out?

Your leverage is the written Atlassian offer. Leverage only exists while the offer is alive and the competing party has not yet decided. Which option uses this leverage before the window closes, without burning the bridge it represents?

Option B uses the Atlassian offer as a catalyst, not as a threat. You tell Razorpay: 'I have a competing offer at ~34L and a 48-hour deadline; Razorpay is my first choice — can you expedite?' If they say yes, you have full information. If they say no, you still have Atlassian. That asymmetry — large upside, minimal downside — is the definition of a good negotiation move.
